item.title: Opinion: Tourism in Central Australia is a victim of the Berrimah Line
item.description: OPINION: Wasteful and scandal ridden Darwin projects such as the Ship Lift and the Waterfront give politicians in the Top End city the ability to claim credit for such developments and enable mates and political supporters to be paid off by an inappropriate and extravagant use of tax-payer funding, while tourism in Central Australia declines, Dr Don Fuller writes.

item.title: Yeperenye Shopping Centre set for $27m redevelopment
item.description: The owners of the Yeperenye Shopping Centre in Alice Springs are planning a $27 million redevelopment of the facility, which will include a new supermarket tenant, and a rooftop restaurant.

item.title: Police executives among three officers issued disciplinary notices for alleged racist comments
item.description: Three senior NT Police officers, including two executives, were issued with serious discipline breach notices for alleged racist comments during a recent senior management meeting, with one of the accused identified as one of five officers who lied in a statutory declaration to the Kumanjayi Walker coronial inquest, sources have told the NT Independent.

item.title: NT Health issues Melioidosis warning as cases ramp up since New Year’s Eve
item.description: The NT Centre for Disease Control has issued urgent alerts for residents and visitors to remain vigilant against melioidosis, following an increase in cases of the soil-borne disease amid recent wet weather in the Top End.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Jan 28
item.description: The 294 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Wednesday, January 28, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: Teen released from custody after arrest for alleged indecent assault
item.description: A 16-year-old male has been released from custody with no charges after he was arrested early Sunday morning in connection to an incident involving a male allegedly entering an Alice Springs home and attempting to indecently assault a female inside, NT Police said.

item.title: ‘Not about one individual’: Pressure mounts on Lia to explain Administrator appointment
item.description: Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro is facing increased political pressure to explain her controversial decision to appoint David Connolly as the NT's next Administrator following national media coverage and growing concerns over his disparaging social media commentary, while not one CLP MLA has voiced public support for the appointment, the NT Independent can reveal.

item.title: New $60m aged care facility operator identified
item.description: Queensland-based not-for-profit Ozcare will build and operate the new $60 million aged care facility in Palmerston, providing 120 to 150 residential beds to alleviate "bed block" in local hospitals, the Prime Minister announced yesterday in Darwin, but it could still be two to three years before the much-needed facility is operational.

item.title: CLP orders all public schools to sing national anthem
item.description: The Finocchiaro CLP Government has mandated that all 152 NT public schools must play and sing the national anthem at assemblies and special events, which Education Minister Jo Hersey said was necessary to "restore national pride".

item.title: ‘Up to them to defend’: PM says he will not overturn CLP’s Administrator pick
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says he is "worried" about whether the CLP Government's pick for Administrator David Connolly is "able to properly represent the Northern Territory in a way which is appropriate" but ruled out overturning the appointment on Tuesday, stating that Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro's government must "explain and defend" its choice.
